mainTopic: Putting water into a hot urn (מיחם) on שבת: the problem of מצרף (hardening the metal), whether the משנה follows רבי שמעון or רבי יהודה on דבר שאין מתכוין, and the dispute between רב and שמואל.
overview: The גמרא asks how the משנה can let a person pour cold water into a hot urn on שבת, since cold water hardens hot metal (מצרף), which is a forbidden מלאכה. The first answer is that the משנה follows רבי שמעון, who permits an unintended result (דבר שאין מתכוין). אביי objects that the משנה's word שפינהו means an urn removed from the fire, not an urn emptied of its water. He rereads the משנה with two cases. If the urn still has hot water, a small amount of cold water may not be added, because it would become fully hot, but a large amount may be added just to warm it. If the urn was emptied, no water may be added at all, because it would harden the metal. That follows רבי יהודה, who forbids an unintended result. Then רב and שמואל argue about the משנה's permission. The גמרא rejects the version in which שמואל permits hardening on purpose and restates their argument as being about the amount of water poured in. שמואל's statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Doesn't pouring cold water harden the urn?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's permission: cold water poured into a hot metal urn hardens the metal (מצרף), which looks like a forbidden מלאכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't this harden the metal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה, which allowed putting cold water into a hot urn. Cold water hitting hot metal hardens it, so how can this be allowed on שבת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Metalworkers pour cold water on hot metal to toughen it, and that is a step in forging. So even if the person only wants warm water, the act seems to cause a forbidden result. The גמרא wants to know why the משנה permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that…? (opens a challenge)
He hardens or tempers the metal by cooling it with water
A metal urn for heating water

phrases.english: But doesn't he harden [the metal]?
phrases.notes: Cold water poured into hot metal toughens it, like a blacksmith's work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the permission given in the משנה (which appears on the previous amud).
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission to put water into a hot urn.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pouring cold water into hot metal causes צירוף, a forbidden מלאכה, so the act should be forbidden.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי שמעון, who permits an unintended result
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the משנה follows רבי שמעון, who holds that דבר שאין מתכוין is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This משנה follows רבי שמעון, who said that an act whose forbidden result is not intended is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי שמעון. He holds that if you do a permitted act and a forbidden result happens without your intending it, the act is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person wants to warm the water, not harden the urn. According to רבי שמעון, an unintended side effect does not make the act forbidden. So the hardening does not matter here.

keyTerms.meaning: This follows the view of רבי שמעון
An act whose forbidden result the person does not intend
Permitted

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of דבר שאין מתכוין (permitted according to רבי שמעון) is a central rule in the laws of שבת and appears throughout ש״ס.

phrases.english: It is [the view of] Rabbi Shimon,
who said: an unintended act is permitted.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to a specific תנא (רבי שמעון).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Hardening the urn should make the act forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Under רבי שמעון, an unintended hardening does not forbid the act.

steps.title: אביי: the משנה's wording does not fit this reading
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that the first answer assumed the משנה speaks of an urn emptied of water. The משנה's word שפינהו means an urn removed from the fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged this: Does the משנה say 'an urn from which water was emptied'? It says 'an urn that was removed' (from the fire)!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks the previous answer by looking closely at the משנה's wording. The first answer read the משנה as speaking of an empty urn, but the משנה's words do not say that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer pictured an empty hot urn being refilled with cold water, which is where hardening becomes a problem. אביי points out that שפינהו means the urn was taken off the fire, while it still has hot water in it. So the case the first answer described is not the משנה's case.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly challenged it
אביי, a leading אמורא
Does it teach…? (rejects a reading of the text)
That he removed it (the urn, from the fire)
That he emptied water out of it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two phrases. שפינהו means the urn was removed from the fire. שפינה ממנו מים means the water was emptied out of the urn. The whole argument depends on this difference.

phrases.english: Abaye strongly objected to it:

phrases.aramaic: מִידֵּי מֵיחַם שֶׁפִּינָּה מִמֶּנּוּ מַיִם קָתָנֵי?!
phrases.english: Does it teach 'an urn from which water was emptied'?!
It teaches 'an urn that was removed [from the fire]'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer in step 2 because it misreads the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading behind the answer that the משנה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's wording speaks of an urn removed from the fire, not an emptied urn, so the case that answer described is not in the משנה.

steps.title: אביי rereads the משנה: an urn removed from the fire that still has hot water
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains the first case of the משנה: an urn removed from the fire with hot water inside. A little cold water may not be added to get hot, but a lot may be added just to become lukewarm.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said this is what the משנה means: An urn removed from the fire that still has hot water in it — one may not put a small amount of water into it to make it hot, but one may put a large amount of water into it to make it lukewarm.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers his own reading of the משנה. This step covers the first case, an urn that still has hot water in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small amount of cold water would become fully hot, which counts as cooking (בישול), so it is forbidden. A large amount only becomes lukewarm, so it is allowed. Here hot water is still in the urn, so the cold water does not hit bare hot metal, and hardening is not the issue.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (a rereading of the text)
A small amount of water
So that they become hot
A large amount of water
To make them lukewarm (take the chill off)

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said, this is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: הַמֵּיחַם שֶׁפִּינָּהוּ וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ מַיִם חַמִּין —
phrases.english: An urn that was removed [from the fire] and has hot water in it —
one may not put a small amount of water into it
so that they become hot,
but one may put a large amount of water into it
in order to make them lukewarm.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading with אביי's own explanation of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה speaks of refilling an emptied urn.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's first case is an urn that still has hot water. The issue there is heating a small amount fully, not hardening.

steps.title: An emptied urn: no water at all, following רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Into an urn emptied of its water, no water at all may be poured because it hardens the metal. So the משנה follows רבי יהודה, who forbids דבר שאין מתכוין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And an urn from which the water was emptied — one may not put any water into it at all, because it hardens the metal. This follows רבי יהודה, who said that an unintended act is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his reading with the second case, an empty hot urn. He concludes that the משנה follows רבי יהודה, the opposite of the first answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the urn is empty, cold water hits the bare hot metal and hardens it. Even though the person does not intend this, רבי יהודה forbids an unintended forbidden result. So the משנה is now assigned to רבי יהודה instead of רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: At all
Because he hardens the metal
רבי יהודה, the תנא who disagrees with רבי שמעון
Forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: The first answer said the משנה follows רבי שמעון, so an unintended act is permitted. אביי says the משנה follows רבי יהודה, so an unintended act is forbidden. Water may be added only when hot water is already in the urn, and an empty hot urn may not be filled at all.

phrases.english: And an urn from which water was emptied —

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִתֵּן לְתוֹכוֹ מַיִם כׇּל עִיקָּר,
phrases.english: one may not put any water into it at all,
because he hardens [the metal].
And it is [the view of] Rabbi Yehuda,
who said an unintended act is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, דְּאָמַר דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּוֵּין אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's rereading and gives its result: which תנא the משנה follows.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to the opposite תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה follows רבי שמעון and permits the hardening.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה forbids water in an emptied urn because of hardening, which follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue about the משנה's permission
steps.stepSummary: רב says the משנה permits only warming, while hardening is forbidden. שמואל says even hardening is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: They only taught this for warming, but for hardening it is forbidden. And שמואל said: Even for hardening it is also permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new argument between רב and שמואל about how far the משנה's permission goes. This begins a new section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב limits the permission to adding water to warm it. שמואל seems to permit it even when the purpose is to harden the urn. That second claim sounds surprising, and the גמרא will challenge it next.

keyTerms.meaning: רב, an early אמורא in בבל
שמואל, רב's frequent partner in debate
They only taught this in the case of… (limits a ruling)
To harden the metal

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְהַפְשִׁיר,
phrases.english: Rav said: They only taught [this] for warming,
but for hardening — it is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ לְצָרֵף נָמֵי מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: And Shmuel said: Even for hardening it is also permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְהַפְשִׁיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion that defines the limits of the משנה's permission.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the permission applies only to warming, and hardening is forbidden. שמואל: even hardening is permitted.

steps.title: Can hardening be permitted from the start?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל's view as reported: how can anyone permit hardening metal on שבת deliberately?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is hardening permitted from the outset?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the report of שמואל's view. Deliberately hardening metal is real מלאכה, so no one could permit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even רבי שמעון only permits a forbidden result that happens without intent. Doing the forbidden act on purpose is never allowed. So שמואל's view cannot have been stated this way.

keyTerms.meaning: From the outset, as a first choice
Is it permitted? (a rhetorical challenge)

phrases.english: Is hardening permitted from the outset?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the version of שמואל's view given in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement that even hardening is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Intentional hardening is a forbidden מלאכה, so it cannot be permitted from the outset.

steps.title: Restating the dispute as about the amount of water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא restates the argument. רב permits only an amount of water that warms and forbids an amount that would harden. שמואל permits even an amount that would harden (his statement continues on the next amud).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said: רב said they only taught an amount that warms, but an amount that would harden is forbidden. And שמואל said: Even an amount that would harden —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by restating רב and שמואל's argument. They are not arguing about intending to harden, only about how much water is poured in. שמואל's sentence finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is now about the amount of water, called the שיעור. רב forbids adding enough water to harden the urn, even when the person only wants to warm it. שמואל permits even that amount, since the person does not intend the hardening.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said (corrects a report)
An amount or measure

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל's sentence is cut off at the end of the amud. His full statement continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated, this is how it was stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שִׁיעוּר לְהַפְשִׁיר,
phrases.english: Rav said: They only taught [this for] an amount that warms,
but an amount that would harden — is forbidden.
And Shmuel said: Even an amount that would harden —
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7 by restating the argument from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the report of the dispute (אי איתמר הכי איתמר).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל permits deliberately hardening the urn.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is about the amount of water poured in, not about intending to harden.
